Position Summary: This role supports project controls and scheduling operations across active transmission, distribution, substation, and renewable energy construction projects throughout the Western United States. Working under the direction of the Project Controls Manager and/or an assigned Senior Scheduler, and in coordination with project managers and field leadership, the Junior Scheduler assists in building, maintaining, and analyzing CPM schedules that reflect real field conditions and contractual obligations. The work is detail-intensive, deadline-driven, and directly tied to project performance — candidates should expect to be challenged and developed quickly. Key Responsibilities What You'll Do Schedule Development & Maintenance Assist in the development of project baseline schedules using Critical Path Method (CPM) logic, incorporating engineering, procurement, permitting, and construction sequences specific to transmission and distribution work Maintain and update project schedules on a weekly and monthly basis, reflecting actual progress, revised sequencing, and current look-ahead windows Build activity logic in Primavera P6, linking predecessors and successors to accurately model field workflows such as structure spotting, excavation, concrete pours, framing, stringing, sagging, and energization milestones Support the development of resource-loaded schedules that align crew deployment plans with project milestones and budgeted labor hours Perform all scheduling work in accordance with Summit Line Project Controls procedures, CPM Technical Standards & Requirements, contractual scheduling specifications, and approved project-specific requirements Schedule Monitoring & Reporting Compare actual progress against baseline and generate variance reports that identify activities with negative float or slippage risk Prepare and distribute two-week look-ahead schedules in coordination with field superintendents and project managers Produce schedule narrative reports for internal project reviews, owner submittals, and monthly progress reporting packages Track key project milestones, contractual completion dates, and owner-imposed interim deadlines, flagging conflicts or risks to the project controls team Collaboration & Field Coordination Work directly with project managers, construction managers, and field superintendents to gather accurate progress data and incorporate field realities into schedule updates Participate in project schedule review meetings, owner progress meetings, and internal project controls calls Coordinate with procurement and materials management teams to incorporate equipment and material lead times — including conductor, transformers, transmission structures, and switchgear — into schedule logic Support the preparation of delay analyses, time impact analyses (TIAs), and schedule recovery plans under the direction of the Project Controls Manager or assigned Senior Scheduler Document Control & Data Integrity Maintain organized schedule files, revision histories, and update logs in accordance with company and client document control requirements Assist in the setup and maintenance of project controls templates and schedule standards across active projects Support project closeout by preparing final as-built schedules and documenting schedule performance metrics Required Qualifications What You'll Bring 1 to 3 years of experience in construction project controls, scheduling, or a comparable support role Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Civil Engineering, Project Management, or a related field — OR equivalent demonstrated experience in a construction project controls or scheduling support role Basic working knowledge of CPM scheduling methodology and schedule logic concepts Foundational working knowledge of Primavera P6, or demonstrated ability to successfully complete Summit Line Primavera P6 training Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel; ability to work with large data sets and perform basic schedule analysis Demonstrated ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, and contract documents Strong attention to detail with the ability to manage multiple concurrent deadlines without loss of accuracy Effective written and verbal communication skills; must be able to work productively with field personnel, project managers, and clients Ability to travel to project sites across the Western U.S. as required — up to 100% travel for certain project assignments Preferred Qualifications Hands-on experience building or updating construction schedules in Primavera P6 Prior internship or work experience with an electrical utility contractor, heavy civil contractor, or specialty subcontractor Familiarity with transmission or distribution construction scopes, including structure installation, conductor stringing, or substation construction sequences Exposure to earned value management (EVM) principles or project cost controls Experience preparing schedule submittals or time impact analyses in a contractor environment PMI Scheduling Professional (PMI-SP), AACE International certification, or active pursuit of same Working knowledge of contract types common to utility construction, including fixed-price, unit-price, and T&M agreements What You'll Get What We Offer Medical, dental, and vision insurance 401(k) retirement plan with company match Paid vacation and company holidays Employer-paid life and disability insurance Direct exposure to large-scale transmission, substation, and renewable energy projects across the Western United States Mentorship from experienced project controls professionals within the Quanta Services network Work Environment This is a primarily office-based role at Summit Line Construction's headquarters in Heber City, Utah, with hybrid flexibility available based on project demands and team needs. However, candidates should enter this role understanding that field visits and extended project site assignments are a genuine part of the job — not an exception to it. Travel requirements can reach up to 100% during active project phases. Project sites are located across the Western U.S. and may include remote transmission corridors, active substation yards, and renewable energy construction facilities. The ability to move between the office environment and active construction sites — and to function effectively in both — is essential to success in this role. Je leert veiligheid en compliance volgens ASME, API en NEN toe te passen, en draagt bij aan detailontwerpen, materiaallijsten en as-built documentatie. Je werkt samen met ervaren engineers en projectmanagers aan projecten in waterstof, stadswarmte en verduurzaming van bestaande installaties. Je gaat aan de slag bij een consultancy- en engineeringkantoor in Schiedam met meerdere vestigingen in Nederland. Het bureau werkt voor klanten in chemie, petrochemie en duurzame energie. De laatste jaren realiseren zij steeds meer projecten in renewable energy, zoals waterstofproductie en verduurzaming van bestaande installaties. Als junior werk je mee aan deze duurzame energieprojecten en krijg je de kans om te leren van ervaren specialisten. Naast grote EPC-projecten ondersteunen zij plant owners in de regio Rotterdam bij onderhouds- en modificatieprojecten. Verwacht afwisseling in projecttypes en -fasen, van studie tot realisatie. Wat ga je doen? Assisteren bij het ontwerpen van ondergrondse leidingsystemen voor duurzame energie, zoals waterstof en stadswarmte; Ondersteunen bij bodemstudies en het opstellen van overzichtstekeningen; Modelleren van pijpleidingen en infrastructuur in AutoCAD en 3D (Plant3D, Civil3D) onder begeleiding van ervaren engineers; Meewerken aan het beoordelen van specificaties en het toepassen van ASME-, API- en NEN-normen; Actief samenwerken met engineers en projectmanagers om ontwerpen te optimaliseren; Bijdragen aan het opstellen van materiaallijsten en as-built tekeningen; Verzamelen van technische documentatie en ondersteunen bij aanbestedingen en offertes. Wat neem je mee? Afgeronde mbo- of hbo-opleiding Civiele Techniek, Werktuigbouwkunde of vergelijkbaar; Affiniteit met duurzame energie en infrastructuur; Basiskennis van CAD-tools zoals AutoCAD, Plant3D, Civil3D en ArcGIS (ervaring is een pré, geen vereiste); Leergierige, proactieve werkhouding en oog voor detail; Flexibiliteit en open houding in wisselende werkomstandigheden; Vloeiend in Nederlands en Engels (schriftelijk en mondeling). Wat bieden we jou? Salaris passend bij een junior functie en jouw opleidingsniveau; Vakantiegeld van 8,33% en minimaal 25 vakantiedagen per jaar; Netto onkostenvergoeding van €500 per jaar; Pensioenregeling en optie tot deelname aan een collectieve zorgverzekering; Gratis opleidingen en trainingen op de eigen Academy, gericht op duurzame energie en technische ontwikkeling; Intensieve begeleiding door een ervaren specialist binnen jouw vakgebied.
